Proposed research claim: Multimodal data fusion improves arc welding defect detection over single-sensor baselines
Evidence available: Step 4 Modality Ablation: Removing sensor features drops F1 from 1.0000 to 0.7407 (RF); removing logs drops F1 to 0.7826. Combining sensor + logs achieves 1.0000.
Limitation: Evaluated purely on synthetic dataset where log fault codes are deterministically injected during anomalies; operator notes provided 0.0000 marginal gain; fusion is tabular concatenation, not joint representation learning.

Proposed research claim: Operator shift notes provide meaningful predictive signal for automated defect detection
Evidence available: Step 4 Modality Ablation: Removing operator notes (WITHOUT_OPERATOR_NOTES) resulted in delta F1 = 0.0000 across all 5 models (RF, LogReg, SVM, IsoForest, DistilBERT).
Limitation: Unstructured text notes generated synthetically via fixed templates; models already achieve ceiling performance on sensor/log features alone; text notes are 100% redundant.

Proposed research claim: Supervised tabular models outperform unsupervised anomaly detection in arc welding
Evidence available: Step 2 & Step 12: Random Forest (F1=1.0000) and Logistic Regression (F1=0.9524) statistically outperform Isolation Forest (F1=0.7096, p=0.0078 and p=0.0156 via exact McNemar test).
Limitation: Holds for this synthetic feature space; unsupervised Isolation Forest suffers from high false positive rate (8 false positives out of 375 test windows).

Proposed research claim: Fine-tuned DistilBERT transformer matches Random Forest performance for industrial welding anomaly detection
Evidence available: Step 6 Model Comparison & Step 12: DistilBERT achieves F1=1.0000, PR-AUC=1.0000, 0 discordant pairs with Random Forest (McNemar p=1.0000).
Limitation: DistilBERT operates on tabular floats serialized into pseudo-natural text strings; requires 100x more compute/latency; totally collapses (F1=0.1818) under trivial prompt serialization shift in Step 5.

Proposed research claim: The proposed system demonstrates high cross-station generalization under Leave-One-Machine-Out validation
Evidence available: Step 1 & Step 12 LOMO CV: RF mean F1 = 0.9683 (CV=5.68%); LogReg mean F1 = 0.9919 (CV=1.42%); DistilBERT mean F1 = 0.9837 (CV=1.43%).
Limitation: All 3 stations were generated from identical synthetic Gaussian distributions with minor drift offsets; station 3 still exhibited measurable degradation (RF dropped to 0.9048); no real physical machines evaluated.

Proposed research claim: The anomaly detection pipeline is robust against factory sensor noise, missing data, and baseline drift
Evidence available: Step 3 Synthetic Robustness: Gaussian noise up to 15%, missingness up to 20%, drift up to 10% maintain RF F1 >= 0.95. Multi-seed runs (n=5) show CV = 0.00% on clean test set.
Limitation: Perturbations were synthetically applied in silico to synthetic signals; does not capture real-world non-Gaussian electromagnetic interference (EMI), torch spatters, sensor disconnects, or varying ambient temperatures.

Proposed research claim: Hybrid RAG (BM25 + Dense) guarantees optimal retrieval performance in industrial welding standards
Evidence available: Step 7 RAG Evaluation: Full hybrid achieves Recall@1=0.875, Recall@3=0.975, Recall@4=1.000, MRR=0.9271 across 40 curated queries and 41 document chunks.
Limitation: 40 hand-curated queries against 41 passages is an artificially small, semi-circular benchmark; K=4 retrieves ~10% of entire corpus; 100% Recall@4 is a sample observation, not a theoretical guarantee (Clopper-Pearson 95% CI is [91.19%, 100.00%]).

Proposed research claim: Intent classification pipeline accurately routes diverse shop-floor operator queries and guards domain boundaries
Evidence available: Step 8 Intent Stress Benchmark: 86.0% accuracy on 100 stress queries across 5 routes (Bootstrap 95% CI [79.0%, 93.0%]); 98.0% binary scope guard accuracy (98/100).
Limitation: Classifier relies primarily on hardcoded keyword lists and regex patterns rather than learned semantic intent models; 100 queries were author-curated; confusion observed between general manufacturing and parameter queries.

Proposed research claim: TreeSHAP provides statistically superior attribution stability compared to LIME in welding diagnostics
Evidence available: Step 9 XAI & Step 12 Statistical Evaluation: Top-5 feature attribution Jaccard stability under 2% noise is 1.000 for SHAP vs 0.928 for LIME (Wilcoxon W=0.0, raw p=0.00031, Holm-adjusted p=0.00155).
Limitation: Demonstrated on tabular Random Forest model across N=60 test windows; establishes algorithmic stability of exact tree-path traversal over stochastic local perturbation sampling.

Proposed research claim: SHAP and LIME feature attributions exhibit statistically proven faithfulness over random feature selection
Evidence available: Step 9 XAI & Step 12 Statistical Evaluation: Feature deletion AUC for SHAP (0.241) and LIME (0.245) vs Random (0.285) yields raw p=0.0495 and p=0.0454.
Limitation: Neither difference survives Holm-Bonferroni family-wise error rate correction (p_adj = 0.13626); SHAP vs LIME deletion difference is also statistically non-significant (p_adj = 0.11038).

Proposed research claim: Self-attention weights from DistilBERT correlate with and validate tabular SHAP feature importance
Evidence available: Step 9 XAI Evaluation Report: Attention is evaluated on subword tokens from unstructured notes; SHAP is evaluated on 40 tabular sensor/log features.
Limitation: Mechanisms operate on completely disjoint feature representations with distinct mathematical targets; cross-method correlation is documented as N/A in repository reports.

Proposed research claim: Physics-based parameter advisor generates optimal, standard-compliant welding settings across all industrial processes
Evidence available: Step 10 Physics Evaluation: 100% exact numerical concordance with closed-form equations (144/144 scenarios); 100% engineering constraint satisfaction (641/641 checks).
Limitation: Calculations represent internal mathematical consistency checks against standard handbook formulas (heat input, deposition rate); zero metallurgical, weld-pool, or mechanical testing (penetration depth, tensile strength, hardness) was conducted.

Proposed research claim: The multimodal architecture achieves sub-20 ms latency suitable for real-time edge deployment in smart factories
Evidence available: Step 11 Deployment Benchmark: Fast deterministic routes achieve median latency of 0.25-17.96 ms (throughput up to 576 QPS).
Limitation: Only true for fast keyword/physics routes; anomaly route requires median 3,300 ms (P95: 3,430 ms) due to rolling feature aggregation and LIME sampling; tested on single-thread local workstation, not distributed factory edge hardware.

Proposed research claim: Linear throughput scaling proves enterprise production scalability for concurrent factory operations
Evidence available: Step 11 Deployment Benchmark: Batch size scaling from N=1 to N=100 showed linear execution time and constant memory footprint.
Limitation: Evaluates sequential single-thread in-memory batch processing; does not measure concurrent multi-user ASGI network requests, database locking, or distributed streaming message queues.

Proposed research claim: The proposed system constitutes a generalizable, physics-informed multimodal foundation for real-world smart manufacturing
Evidence available: Broad thesis and project claim throughout README and documentation.
Limitation: Evaluated exclusively on synthetic tabular data with 60 injected anomalies across 3 simulated stations; physics module is a decoupled formula calculator; no real industrial trials, physical weld specimens, or human operator evaluations exist.
